The concept of the game is quite interesting; it's not the usual boring battle royale. You have to recruit heroes with perks and weapons and fight on a big PvEvP map with dynamic objectives.

The problem lies in the fact that perks are extremely uninspired and hardly noticeable in the game. There are dozens of weapons that all feel basically the same, the UI is cluttered, and the gameplay is overall extremely frustrating. Essentially, you either die because of a suspicious 100-meters headshot from a low MMR player who was camping for no reason in the middle of nowhere or because other teams simply rushed harder than you did. Yes, rush. Rushing seems to be king in a game specifically designed to punish players who make too much noise by breaking sticks on the floor or fighting with zombies. Does that make perfect sense, right?

It's fine if you intend to play casually with a friend or two, and if you can grab this for 10 bucks. But expect to be frustrated and lost inside this mess of a game.

Great engine and content facelift. It does CS2's update better than CS2. If it were only based off that, this review would be positive.

However the UI is an abomination. I haven't seen anything anywhere this bad. The main menu is full screen advertisements for skin bundles in an already pay to play game. Side tabs are inconsistent, hotkeys change between menus, and buttons linking the battlepass are shoved everywhere.

The worst part is that it takes 20+ clicks to recruit and equip a hunter. Each hunter comes with ten slots, and each slot means a full screen transition into an unsorted grid that doesn't save sort filters. Your owned skins are randomly mixed in with unowned skins, and an errant double click means you're out $5-15 in premium currency. It's insane how bad it is.

You'd think the worst part of dying in an extraction shooter is losing your perks and gear. Instead it's the prospect of clicking through 30 screens just to get geared up and playing again.

It's incredible how bad the UI is.

At 500 hours, I feel able to give a reasonable-enough review for folks looking into this game.
Hunt is unforgiving. The first dozen or so matches (maybe 5-10 hours) will be complete shocks and chaos. Their tutorial is not great; if anything, it teaches you how NOT to play the game well. But if you have a friend who's familiar with the game, or if you watch a few streamers/YouTubers, you'll quickly get a feel for this game.
It's fun, edge-of-your-seat, brutally realistic action (as in, one bullet from someone you don't see or hear ends your match). It's a game about stealth, movement, and strategy.
The weapons all feel well-balanced. You can kill just as effectively with your starting guns (if not better) than the final-unlock automatic rifles and semi-modern tech handguns.
Crytex listens to the community, they don't craft cheap DLC to belch out (I've bought most of it) just for the money. There's arguments that some skins are "PAY TO WIN" because they might disappear into the forests better. I find this is generally untrue for seasoned players, and feel like the devs are working ahrd to keep the community happy and the game thriving.

If you are the type of person who got this far looking into Hunt - I think you're probably the kind of person who would enjoy it. Give it more than 1-5 games to get used to it. Remember, you don't win - you just live to die another day.

tldr.text: Mostly Positive (76%): players praise the gameplay and combat.
The most common complaint is the developers and their updates, followed by bugs and crashes.

details.text: Recent reviews complain far less about updates and bugs than before, but cheaters now come up more often.
A negative review wave, often called a review bomb, pulled one month down to 51% positive from a usual 74%, so check recent reviews before buying.

reason.text: Negative reviews from this period mostly object to the new menu UI that came with the 1896 update, which reviews describe as harder to navigate than the old one.
Some reviews also report stutters, crashes, and connection problems, which they present as separate from the menu complaints.
